## How the guide defines it

p. 2: `SS – Schedule Strength`.

## How the guide uses it

Every conference table prints a schedule strength figure and a national rank out of 138 for every team. The win-total feature rests 17 of its 29 bets on the schedule, and several contributors argue almost entirely from it — Pauly Howard bets Penn State Over while stating he is not a fan of the head coach, purely because the slate avoids Oregon, Ohio State and Indiana.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

A single figure summarising the quality of the opponents on a team's schedule, ranked against all 138.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the second half of every win-total projection. A rating says how good a team is; schedule strength says what that quality will be asked to do. The guide's largest win-total-versus-rating gaps are almost entirely schedule effects.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Two ways. As a printed rank in the tables, and as a walked argument in prose, where a contributor goes game by game and counts the losses they can find — Makinen's method on UNLV and Boise State.

## Where it appears

Every conference preview table; pp. 22–27 for the walked arguments; p. 46 for how it enters the method.
